_readme: ADVERSARIAL SEED for the ClaimableItems group. TEMPORARY - deleted in Step 08.
Captured through the MOUNTED HOST, not a sample host - this group ships none. That is one
notch weaker than the other two groups and the limitation is real: consumer middleware order,
request localization, CORS, fallback routing and any host-level JSON options are NOT
reproduced, so a behaviour change hiding in host wiring rather than in the module will not be
caught here.
ID BLOCKS, chosen so no row's PK ever equals a foreign id it carries:
Campaign          7_000_00x
ClaimableItem     7_010_00x
CampaignVinEntry  7_020_00x
Certificate       7_030_00x   (dbo schema - owned by ADP.Cases, shared with WarrantyClaims)
ItemClaim         7_040_00x   <- the group's one true link row
TRAP COVERAGE, confirmed against code then adversarially re-checked:
trap2  ItemClaim as a CHILD of ItemClaimCertificateDTO.ReimbursementItemClaims. ItemClaim
is this group's link row: its own PK plus CampaignID, ClaimableItemID,
CampaignVinEntryID and two certificate FKs. Seeded so ALL of them differ, so any
wrong projection emits a well-formed hash id of a real row of the wrong entity -
which nothing short of a literal comparison distinguishes from correct.
trap3write  Certificate.CertificateNo - a live production numbering sequence, insert-only
guarded. Seeded 999001, a value the sequence could not reach.
trap3write  Certificate.DisplayDistributorCertificateNo - same guard, but a STRING, which
makes it the single clearest probe in the group: a sentinel appearing in a readback
is unmistakable.
trap3write  ItemClaim.ClaimNumber - the per-(CompanyID, ClaimableItemID) sequential claim
identifier, derived rather than client-supplied. Seeded 4242.
trap1 / trap3read  NOT present in this group and deliberately not faked. Soft-deleted rows
are still seeded so the framework's global IsDeleted filter stays covered.
TABLE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Keys beginning with _ are harness metadata, never written to SQL.
DATA-LEVEL ACCESS SCOPING: rows carry CompanyID/CountryID/CompanyBranchID = 1, matching the
parity principal's claims. A mismatch does not error - the list simply returns
{"Count":0,"Value":[]} with a 200, so the baseline looks healthy and proves nothing.
The hostile-row gate is what caught this.
STATUS: this seed is AUTHORED AND APPLIES CLEANLY (7 rows) but the group is NOT yet
captured. Every entity carrying a CompanyID column lists as {"Count":0,"Value":[]} under
the mounted host regardless of whether those columns are 1 or NULL, while ServiceCampaign
(no CompanyID column) lists correctly. The remaining suspect is TypeAuth DYNAMIC-action
data-level access: the parity access tree grants static levels [1,2,3,4] but no explicit
accessible-id set, so a dynamic action resolves to an empty set and filters everything out.

rows._why: Soft-deleted. Must never appear in a list body - the global IsDeleted filter. No _marker: its ABSENCE is the assertion.
rows.Name: PARITY-CAMPAIGN-SOFTDELETED must-not-appear
PARITY-CLAIMABLEITEM parity claimable item
rows._why: Belongs to campaign 7000001. The list DTO maps CampaignName from src.Campaign!.Name - a NON-NULLABLE navigation dereference - so a ClaimableItem with no campaign makes the whole list 500 with 'Nullable object must have a value'. Seed the relationship, do not leave it dangling.
The marker doubles as the VIN so it is matchable literally in a list body. PK 7020001 differs from CampaignID 7000001.

CertificateNo 999001 and DisplayDistributorCertificateNo are BOTH insert-only, sequence-derived columns the reverse map must not write. A write body sends different values; a readback carrying them proves the trap fired. Note dbo schema: Certificate belongs to ADP.Cases and is shared with WarrantyClaims - the same entity is mapped by a triple in each group (SPIKE-8).

THE LINK ROW. Own PK 7040001; CampaignID 7000001; ClaimableItemID 7010001; CampaignVinEntryID 7020001; ReimbursementCertificateID 7030001. Every number distinct, so any wrong projection into a child ID is a visible diff rather than a coincidence. ClaimNumber 4242 is the derived per-company sequential identifier - a write body sending a different number must not change it.
SOFT-DELETED sibling claim on the SAME certificate. Any child collection over reimbursement claims must exclude it.
